positions.name: KestrelwoodCalibrationStatus
positions.frame: What is the verified calibration state of the Kestrelwood spectrograph, and on what standard does that verification rest?
positions.why: All three expressions assert the same underlying fact — the instrument calibrated at 88.4 MHz, verified against the June reference plates — from the same authoritative, informational footing (Quill Ashgrove as animator/author/principal throughout). src-1 states it in prose with a completed-verification frame ('verified... holds across the full observing band'); src-2 and src-3 restate the identical content as structured labeled fields ('**Instrument**', '**Calibration**'). The directional reads converge: technical/matter-of-fact register, authority-ranking relational stance (citing the June plates as the standard being deferred to), expert/informational power stance, and competence as the appealed-to value — the prose and the header format are two performances of one claim whose truth rests on the calibration state itself, not on anything beyond the words. No tension: all three pull the same direction, differing only in surface format (narrative sentence vs. field label).
